[33m#S3[0m Cookie library: make stringifySetCookie reject maxAge over 400 days (34,560,000 seconds) with a TypeError, with tests and README updated (Nov 3, 7:29 AM)


[34mInvestigated:[0m The cookie repo's maxAge handling in src/index.ts, the README maxAge section, and the existing maxAge tests in src/stringify-set-cookie.spec.ts and src/parse-set-cookie.spec.ts. The stringify path previously checked only that maxAge was an integer, and parse accepted any Max-Age value, including negatives.

[33mLearned:[0m stringifySetCookie previously emitted any integer maxAge as "; Max-Age=N" with no upper bound. Browsers cap cookie lifetimes at 400 days, so larger values were silently shortened. Parsing of incoming Max-Age headers is separate and remains unbounded.

[32mCompleted:[0m src/index.ts now defines a 400-day constant and throws TypeError "option maxAge is too large (max 34560000): <value>" when maxAge exceeds it. The check runs after the integer check. The maxAge JSDoc was updated. The README maxAge section documents the 400-day limit. src/stringify-set-cookie.spec.ts gained tests for 34,560,000 (accepted) and 34,560,001 (throws). The vitest run passed 63,742 tests across 4 files, tsc --noEmit reported no errors, and git diff shows 3 files changed with 27 insertions. Nothing has been committed.

[35mNext Steps:[0m No further work is in progress. The changes are uncommitted in the working tree and await review or a commit instruction from the user.

[36mNotes:[0m Negative maxAge values are not bounded by this change, and parseSetCookie still accepts any incoming Max-Age value. Only the stringify side enforces the cap, as requested.
